artifacts.summary: Establishes that /revise is unreachable from a dispatched agent for two compounding reasons (structural command->skill->agent unidirectionality, and an unsanctioned direct skill-reviser path that would skip GATE IN/OUT), and recommends documenting the unavailability plus the existing state-write.sh Stage 7 description-update fallback on both commands/revise.md and skills/skill-reviser/SKILL.md, rejecting postflight-tool-restrictions.md as the home.

memory_candidates.content: commands/revise.md and skills/skill-reviser/SKILL.md document no agent-unavailability note despite /revise being structurally unreachable from a dispatched subagent (creating-commands.md's command->skill->agent flow has no reverse arrow) and skill-reviser itself being unsanctioned for direct invocation (it is not user-only like skill-tag, but direct invocation skips commands/revise.md's GATE IN task-lock acquisition and GATE OUT .return-meta.json cleanup). The correct fallback for a dispatched agent updating a sibling task's description is skill-reviser/SKILL.md's own Stage 7 'For Description Update' state-write.sh object-merge block, already verified correct by a live incident (884, iss_1793913745294_dZNuX5).

postflight-tool-restrictions.md's scope is the skill-postflight-phase tool boundary (what a postflight script may do after a subagent returns), audience 'Skill authors, /meta agent, system maintainers' -- it is the WRONG home for a statement about what a dispatched AGENT may invoke mid-execution (a different actor, different lifecycle point). Point-of-use documentation on the actual surfaces an agent will meet (e.g. commands/revise.md, skill-reviser/SKILL.md) is the established pattern in this codebase, mirroring how the AskUserQuestion withholding is documented at agent-frontmatter-standard.md and push-consent-relay.md rather than in a generic registry.
